language.howToChooseYourGradeIntro: Our curriculum Grades K to 6 corresponds with ages:
language.howToChooseYourGradeContent:
It’s very important children start at the right level, have fun in learning and work at their own pace. Please help the children selecting the level that is not too easy, but also not too difficult for them. There are two ways to do this.

  • You can either check the learning goals yourself to determine the correct level for your child(ren).
  • Or you can let the child take several lessons to determine his or her level. For example, if your child has the age of 6, please let him or her take one lesson in grade K, one lesson in grade 1, and one lesson in grade 2 to determine at which level he or she is.

dialog.text: Hi! My name is Emilio. I'm on this pirate ship in the middle of the Caribbean Ocean because I like Pirates. They sailed through the seas searching for treasures and making things happen. They had rules called "the code" which helped them to do their work.

The ability to make things happen is one way to describe energy. Just like pirates, energy has to follow a code, which is a type of law. Energy follows the "Law of Conservation." This law of energy states that energy can never be created or destroyed. It can only change. And that's what this lesson is about.
Hi there! My name is Tim. I'm here to help Emilio learn about energy conversion and how energy conversion makes things happen.

Hi there! My name is Tim. I'm here to help Emilio learn about energy conversion and how energy conversion makes things happen.
There are two types of energy: potential and kinetic. Potential energy is the energy an object has because of its shape or position.
Kinetic energy is the energy an object has because of its motion. So remember: potential energy is stored energy and kinetic energy is energy at work.
